Subject: Onramp latchpoint & evidence playbook — MSA/DPA sequencing

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. To keep momentum on the pilot procurement, I put together a short "latchpoint" proposal so we can parallelize onboarding work without exposing either side to unnecessary legal risk. Attached is a working MAP (Novasec_MAP_v3.xlsx) that maps evaluation milestones to procurement/legal gates. Quick summary: 

- Goal: enable orderform signature to occur while certain DPA redlines continue in legal review, but only if a short evidence checklist is provided up front.
- Core ask from Novasec: confirmation of SOC2 or equivalent evidence, subprocessor list, and a limited set of DPA clause outcomes.
- Proposed sequencing (high level): MSA sign -> Orderform execute (latchpoint) -> DPA finalized within 10 business days OR specific mitigations in place.

Can Laura and Vanessa weigh in on which DPA clauses absolutely must be closed pre-orderform versus which can be staged? If Novasec's procurement team can get us SOC2 summary and subprocessor list this week, we may be able to hit a Dec 1 order signature and provisioning week of Dec 7.

I've attached the MAP and a draft set of DPA redlines for context.

Next steps:
1) Confirm evidence checklist (Novasec provides)
2) Legal to confirm latchable clause set (Laura)
3) Agree target signature date and order provisioning window

Thanks,
Karthik

Appreciate the clear framing and the MAP. Procurement and legal will need to see the SOC2 Type II report or an attestation summary, plus an up-to-date subprocessor list. Two quick notes from our side: 

- Procurement prefers all legal docs (MSA + DPA) fully executed before Purchase Order if risk profile > medium. We can be flexible for pilots if compensating controls are in place.
- Our legal team flagged audit rights and cross-border data transfer language in the redlines you shared; those are likely blockers unless we get clarifying language or an interim mitigation.

Thanks for the context, all. I reviewed the MAP and the redlines; below is a pragmatic sequencing we recommend for a pilot while protecting both parties.

Recommended sequencing (detailed):
1) MSA: finalize and sign. Must be executed before orderform.
2) DPA: for pilots we can accept an "Orderform latchpoint" under the following conditions (these must be confirmed pre-orderform):
   - SOC2 Type II report or SOC2 summary provided and scoped to hosting/data processing controls.
   - Subprocessor list provided with commitment to notify and remediate critical changes within 30 days.
   - Audit rights language: agree to a mutually scoped audit approach (we can accept attestation vs full audit for pilot).
   - Data residency and international transfer controls: confirm the region and any restrictions; if transfers are required, propose SCCs or equivalent mitigations in writing.
   - Any indemnity or liability carve-outs that materially change risk allocation must be resolved pre-signature.

3) Orderform execution: allowed at latchpoint if (a) MSA is signed, (b) required evidence above is submitted, and (c) Novasec acknowledges DPA will be finalized within 10 business days (DocuSign link to post-sign redline flow).
4) Post-orderform: Redwood to provision baseline capacity and begin non-production data syncs. Full production onboarding contingent on DPA execution.

I attached a short checklist inline with the MAP for procurement to tick off. If Novasec can provide SOC2 summary and subprocessor list by 11/30, I will route the DPA redlines through our legal queue and aim to close the outstanding items by 12/10. 

Proposed target dates (for clarity):
- Evidence submission deadline: 2026-11-30
- Orderform signature (latchpoint): 2026-12-01
- Initial provisioning: week of 2026-12-07
- DPA finalization deadline: 2026-12-14 (10 business days from orderform)

Happy to join the Tue 11/24 call; otherwise we can run this asynchronously.

Thanks,
Laura

- We agree to the orderform latchpoint on 2026-12-01 provided the evidence is delivered and MSA language is accepted.

Assuming that, procurement will issue the PO and we will target initial provisioning the week of 12/07. David in Ops will coordinate on the provisioning checklist after PO.
